steps.title: Read the denial and the deadline
steps.detail: Read the denial letter: Home health physical therapy, 12 visits over 6 weeks, denied on 2026-10-20; appeal by 2026-12-24.

steps.title: Pull supporting notes from the records
steps.detail: Pulled 7 relevant items from the records (visits, results, medicines). Nothing is added that isn't on file.

steps.title: Get a letter of medical necessity from the doctor
steps.detail: Called Harbor Light Internal Medicine at (555) 010-0211: pressed 4 (medical records), then transferred to the doctor's medical assistant, waited 15 minutes on hold, reached Rob, the doctor's medical assistant. The doctor will sign the letter and the office will fax it. Reference R-17296.

steps.title: Match the evidence to the plan's rules
steps.detail: Mapped 16 pieces of evidence to the plan's 4 rules: 3 met, 1 partly.

steps.title: Write the appeal
steps.detail: Appeal letter drafted, with the doctor's letter, records and a criteria table attached.

steps.title: Stress-test the appeal
steps.detail: Stress-tested: the insurer-side reviewer went over it 2 times; the writer answered its objections in 1 revision, and the last review found no reason to deny.

steps.title: Fax it to the plan and confirm it arrived

review.original:
I'm appealing the denial of home health physical therapy, which was denied because the plan says it isn't medically necessary.
I have asked my doctor, Dr. Samuel Okafor (Harbor Light Internal Medicine), for a letter of medical necessity (office reference R-17296); the office will send it to you directly. The enclosed records show the history behind the request. Each of the plan's coverage criteria is answered in the enclosed table.

Please send me the plan's decision in writing, and a copy of the criteria used.

objections.rule: The member is homebound: leaving home takes a considerable and taxing effort.
objections.reason: The letter does not make the case that leaving home takes a considerable and taxing effort and does not name any supporting evidence for homebound status.
objections.needs: A point in the letter that the member is homebound and a citation to the Physical therapy evaluation (2026-10-10) showing walker, one-person assist and taxing effort to leave home

objections.rule: A doctor has certified a plan of care for the therapy.
objections.reason: The letter does not identify a certified plan of care and only references a future letter from Dr. Okafor (R-17296) that has not been sent.
objections.needs: A citation in the letter to the Home health plan of care certified and signed by Dr. Samuel Okafor for physical therapy 12 visits (2026-10-14) on file

objections.rule: Skilled therapy is needed to restore or keep the member's function.
objections.reason: The letter does not explain that skilled therapy is needed to restore or keep function and does not cite evidence showing that need.
objections.needs: A point that skilled therapy can restore declined balance and walking and a citation to the Physical therapy evaluation (2026-10-10)

objections.rule: The services are reasonable and necessary for the member's condition.
objections.reason: The letter does not address why home services are reasonable and necessary for the condition versus outpatient therapy.
objections.needs: A point that outpatient therapy is not safe due to fall risk and a citation to the Doctor's note (2026-10-14) and the PT evaluation showing need for skilled therapy

revision.body:
Dear Appeals Unit at Bluewater Health:

I am Rosa Rivera, member ID BWM-77031882, Bluewater Medicare Advantage HMO, and I am appealing the denial on 2026-10-20, case SIM-PA-20431, of home health physical therapy as not medically necessary.

I meet each coverage rule:

1. I am homebound and leaving home takes a considerable and taxing effort. I stopped driving last year. My physical therapy evaluation on 2026-10-10 states I need a walker and one person's help to leave home and that leaving home takes a taxing effort. My doctor's note on 2026-10-14 states outpatient therapy isn't safe for me right now because of fall risk on stairs and in transit.

2. A doctor has certified a plan of care for the therapy. My home health plan of care was certified and signed by Dr. Samuel Okafor, Harbor Light Internal Medicine, for physical therapy, 12 visits, on 2026-10-14. I have also asked Dr. Okafor for a letter of medical necessity, office reference R-17296, and the office will send it to you directly.

3. Skilled therapy is needed to restore or keep my function. I had an emergency visit after a fall at home on 2026-04-03. My physical therapy evaluation on 2026-10-10 states my balance and walking have declined since the fall and skilled therapy can restore them.

4. The home services are reasonable and necessary for my condition. The certified plan of care from Dr. Okafor prescribes 12 visits of physical therapy in the home, the evaluation ties that therapy to restoring my declined balance and walking, and the doctor's note states outpatient therapy isn't safe right now because of fall risk on stairs and in transit.

The enclosed records show the history behind the request. Please send me your written decision on this appeal, and a copy of the criteria used.

facts.core_argument: For home health physical therapy, the file has strong proof on three rules and a gap on the fourth. A therapy evaluation says leaving home takes a taxing effort and needs a walker and another person's help, and a doctor's note says therapy outside the home is not safe right now due to fall risk on stairs and in travel. A doctor signed a plan for 12 home visits, and the evaluation ties the need to worse balance and walking since a fall, with skilled therapy able to restore them. The weak spot is detail on why 12 visits is the right amount for her condition.
